name: App shell
summary: How an AhaSlides product SCREEN is assembled from DS components — the left nav rail (real brand mark + nav items + one primary CTA), the top bar (context left, actions/avatar right), the content region, and where relevant a canvas/stage — spaced by --aha-* tokens, with a real brand identity and no dead placeholders. Closes the composition gap that turns a component-correct screen into generic-admin-template slop.
highlights: How a product screen is assembled from DS components
Left nav rail, top bar, content region and optional canvas, spaced by --aha-* tokens
Real brand identity, no dead placeholders
Closes the gap between component-correct and generic admin template
lead: The DS ships no shell/nav/rail leaf, so a consumer hand-rolls the screen scaffold — and hand-rolled scaffold is where slop enters: a placeholder letter-tile logo, a 'Loading…' block shipped as final, evenly-spaced equal-weight cards. This pattern ships NO new component; it documents how to compose the shell from existing DS components and binds each rule to a binary criterion the consumer self-judges.

skillRef.note: Authored in the DS. The DS OWNS this surface's criteria in anti-slop/criteria.json (surfaces.app-shell, C1..C6); the plugin's aha-design skill builds and judges against them.

composedOf.use: the top-left brand of the header or nav rail: The Splash, AhaSlides and the product name as one mark
the primary CTA in the nav rail (e.g. New presentation), top-bar actions, and per-row actions — one primary per region, sized via the size prop, never inline height/padding/radius
the brand mark glyph, every nav-item glyph, and top-bar action glyphs — an <aha-icon name> from the library, never an inline <svg> or a foreign icon set
the top-bar account avatar and any per-row user avatar
the 'New' marker on a nav item or menu row
the name plus shortcut chip on every presenter control-bar button (shortcut attribute), so the key is shown where the control is
the active/selected nav-item transition duration — toggled on a persistent node, never a bare literal
the radius on rail/top-bar/content surfaces — from the 4/6/8/12/16 scale

componentBacklog: No missing components — the shell composes entirely from shipped DS leaves plus tokens. The gap this pattern closes is COMPOSITION knowledge, not a missing primitive.

rules.rule: The top-left brand of any site, microsite or app header, nav rail included, is <aha-product-lockup product="<name>"> (no product attribute when no name is approved): full above a 480px header, compact below, variant="splash" in an icon rail. Never hand-set The Splash or the logo file next to a text span, and never a coloured letter tile or initials square standing in for a logo; every other logo comes from the Logo library (design.ahaslides.io/foundations/logo.html), or for a third-party brand from the Brands tab of the Icon library (design.ahaslides.io/icons/index.html?tab=brands).
Never ship a placeholder as a final state: a QR/thumbnail/region renders a real asset or an explicit, styled empty state — never a permanent 'Loading QR…' label, spinner, or grey box.
Give each region one primary action and a scannable type hierarchy from the scale; do not render uniform grey-on-white equal-weight cards with evenly-spaced everything (the admin-template tell).

Fill every shell slot with a DS component (aha-button, aha-icon, aha-avatar, aha-badge, DataTable) and take all spacing/radius/colour from --aha-* tokens — never a hand-rolled <button>/<div> with inline hex/px, never a raw <table>.

Animate the active/selected nav state by toggling an attribute/class on a persistent node via the motion tokens (--aha-motion-* + --aha-ease-*); never snap, never a bare duration literal, never rebuild the subtree on selection.

On the presenting view, every host control (each presenter control-bar button, manifest-declared slide actions included, each popover, picker or menu one opens, and each host layer drawn over the live slide, such as ink annotation and its toolbar) is judged here, never left to the canvas review. Every presenter control-bar button has its key in its tooltip (<aha-tooltip size="lg" text="Annotate" shortcut="D">, aria-label `Annotate (D)`), and the popover it opens takes focus on open and returns it to the trigger on close. Esc closes an open popover before it can reach exit-presenting, and every control-bar key is listed in the presenter hotkey cheatsheet (K) on a panel that sits next to its control, joined to it by the same line and dot as the existing panels (Back to Editor, QR code, Confetti), and stays joined as the control bar changes; a floating or corner-pinned panel fails even when the key and name match. The shortcut chip is the canvas C10 chip (24 × 24, radius 4); the host sizes and themes the control itself, never with applyCanvasDeck or the in-canvas size="lg" rule. Prove it by pressing the keys in the real UI and recording each result, plus screenshots of the whole presenting screen with the cheatsheet open, at rest and after a bar change; reading the code is not proof.

reuseNote: Doc-only pattern — the DS ships no shell wrapper leaf. The composition lives in the consuming app; this pattern is the conventions + the binary criteria (anti-slop/criteria.json → surfaces.app-shell) a consumer self-judges against.

selfCheck.label: real brand mark + wordmark, no placeholder letter-tile
no dead 'Loading…' placeholder shipped as final; real asset or explicit empty state
one primary action per region; scannable hierarchy, not equal-weight cards
every slot is a DS component; all spacing/radius/colour from tokens; no raw table
active nav state animates on a persistent node via motion tokens

presenter control bar: key in every tooltip, popover focus in and back, Esc closes the popover before exit-presenting, every key in the cheatsheet on a panel joined to its control by the line and dot, from a recorded keyboard run and cheatsheet screenshots
